title: Sharing GPUs: batch work borrows serving's idle GPU and gives it back
design_ref: Sharing GPUs between training and inference
purpose: Run a resumable batch job on the GPU serving is not using. When serving needs that GPU, Kueue must take it back, serving must come up on it, and the batch job must later resume where it stopped.

steps.display: kubectl create -f batch-job.yaml   # batch-resumable: 80 items of GPU work (about 5 s each), queue batch, no GPU quota of its own
kubectl get clusterqueue serving batch   # who uses and who borrows
kubectl -n batch-eval get workload   # the borrower's Workload

checks.description: the batch job is running on a GPU it borrowed from the serving queue
checks.because: Batch owns no GPU quota. Serving owns two, uses one, and may lend one.

checks.description: when serving scaled up, Kueue preempted the batch job to take the GPU back
checks.because: Serving's queue is within its own quota and reclaimWithinCohort is Any, so a borrower is the first thing to go.

checks.description: serving got its second GPU and the replica is ready
checks.because: Kueue gave the replica the quota the batch Workload released.

checks.description: the batch job was requeued, not lost
checks.because: Kueue suspends the Job and keeps its Workload in the queue.

checks.description: when serving scaled back down the batch job was admitted again and resumed from its saved progress, not from item 0
checks.because: It read its progress from S3 and continued at item 11.

checks.description: the batch job completed all its items
checks.because: Preemption cost it a restart, not its progress.
